outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py: `_status_events` now carries each change's origin (`_row_origin`: actor.via, sessionId/envSessionId, the journal file read_all tagged, the action). `_status_chain` returns (chain, unaccounted) and folds a repeat with no span only when `_echoes` proves it the journal-writes hook's record of the row before it: a hook row after a named non-hook writer's row (cli/drive verb) of the same from/to under a shared session name (its edit row, or a derived task.blocked/task.complete when the edit row's changes list was clipped - seen in the real journal at 2026-10-16T18:38:06Z, 12 changes kept), or a derived row straight after its own hook edit row in the same file under the same sessions. A closing no-from row (wave.done) between the verb and the echo neither changes the chain nor separates them. Any other repeat leaves the span from the repeated row to itself; `_ran_within` answers None for a window touching a span unless a recorded change inside the window says running (the kept attempt's reading, kept). `_ordered_seconds`: a second whose rows came from more than one journal file is read only when every row records the same change (then the non-hook rows go first so an echo follows its source); two different changes there make the chain None. Time is never read. Rule derived from hooks/journal-writes.py (`_actor` via 'hook', `_manifest_rows` primary + chained rows with dict(row['actor']), `_append_rows` appends them in order; `_swept_tree` nulls sessionId when a peer is live - such a row proves nothing and keeps the charge) and from the real journal (cli task.block/task.start/task.done/wave.done rows, hook manifest.edit/task.blocked/task.complete echoes, all status rows carry a sessionId). tests/test_audit_task.py: hw15/hw16 taken from refs/audit/kept/P142.35-6yq unchanged; hw17-hw20 new.
